The two dim ink tokens — now vs proposed

--text-faint and --text-dim are alphas, so what they measure depends on the glass under them. At their current values --text-faint composites to between 2.71:1 and 2.97:1 against the real backgrounds of the six tabs, against a 4.5:1 bar for body text. It is not a decorative token: it carries every form label, every table header, and the whole of the empty states.

The proposed values are not a level invented for this. Monthly already hardcodes #93A2B8 and #8695AB for its own labels, headers and empty states — #EAF0FA at roughly alpha .64 and .58 — and measures 5.4:1 to 7.1:1 there. One tab had met the bar by hand; this brings the other five up to it. Hue, weight, size and layout are untouched.

now  --text-faint .35  /  --text-dim .55
proposed  --text-faint .58  /  --text-dim .74
across the six tabs  65 → 20 failing specs

That 65 → 20 is one instrument measured on both builds at 1440px: ancestor backgrounds and gradients composited down onto the page, background-clip:text read as ink rather than as backdrop, transitions frozen, and the Plan tab seeded so its rows render. 15 of the remaining 20 are the Plan tab, which this change does not touch and which needs its own pass.

Nothing in the app was edited to make this page. Both halves of every pair are the live app at the same viewport and scroll position, with the proposed values injected through page.addStyleTag(), which lands after the app's own :root and wins on source order. The crops are screenshots rather than copied markup because these inks are painted over backdrop-filtered glass — a fragment lifted out of the page composites against something else.
